nahhas-irab:1-1.t: What is well known in the language is that al-ḍuḥā is the first rising of the sun when it shines forth, even though Mujāhid said: al-ḍuḥā is the daytime, and that is the view of al-Farrāʾ.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
"…and (has failed whose soul He) led astray". Qatāda said: he has succeeded who purified his soul with righteous deeds. Abū Jaʿfar said: In this there is an obscure point of grammar that al-Farrāʾ did not mention, even though he mentioned the two views on the meaning. It is that if the pronoun refers back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, nothing from its ṣila (relative clause) refers back to من except through a far-fetched device. That is because if you take it as "the person who purified the soul has succeeded", nothing from its ṣila refers back to الذي; and if you take it as "the person whose soul Allah purified has succeeded", it is not permissible to use a pronoun for the soul, because nothing refers back to the soul. And if you took «من» as standing for the soul, it would be far-fetched, because من hardly occurs in the like of this. The device by which it is permissible is to construe it according to the meaning: that «من» is treated as feminine in the sense of "the soul", or that the meaning is "the group whom Allah purified has succeeded", so that «من» is for the plural. The meaning of "Allah purified it" is: He cleansed it by granting success to obey Him.
And "so-and-so purified (zakkā) his wealth": concerning its derivation there are two views. One of them is that it is from zakā al-zarʿ, when the crop increases and grows, i.e., his wealth became abundant through his paying the zakāt. The other view, which is clear and good, is that zakkā his wealth means he purified it and cleared it by taking out the shares of the poor from it. From this is أَقَتَلْتَ نَفْساً زَكِيَّةً [al-Kahf: 74], i.e., pure, cleansed of sins; and from it, "a pure servant (ʿabd zakiyy)", i.e., clean.
«وقد خاب», i.e., he did not attain what he wanted, whose soul Allah corrupted (dassā), i.e., abandoned it so it committed sins. And on the other view, "who corrupted his soul", i.e., concealed it for committing sin. Its derivation is from dassa and dassasa, and one of the two sīns was changed into a yāʾ, as the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 568- رأت رجلا أيما إذا الشّمس عارضت ("She saw a man who, whenever the sun faced him…"), meaning أمّا.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِطَغْواها (11): al-ṭaghwā and al-ṭughyān (transgression) are one, except that ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: بطغواها means "by its punishment", al-ṭaghwā being a name for the punishment. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is valid on the basis of an omission, i.e., "by the punishment of its transgression", like وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [Yūsuf: 82].

nahhas-irab:12-12.t:
Al-Farrāʾ reported that they were two, and he recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 569-
ألا بكّر النّاعي بخيري بني أسد ... بعمرو بن مسعود وبالسّيّد الصّمد
(The announcer of death came early with news of the two best of Banū Asad: ʿAmr ibn Masʿūd and the lofty chief.)
He means that he made خير (a singular form) the predicate for two, and he likened it to their saying: "these two are the most excellent of people" and "these two are the best of people". Abū Jaʿfar said: What he reported is contrary to what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said, what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, and what the exegetes said. Allah said: أشقاها, informing about one, yet he reported that they were two. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A man volunteered for it", and he did not say "two men". And the exegetes said: Qudār ibn Sālif volunteered for it. Abū Jaʿfar said: He has a parallel to it, or something greater than it, in Sūrat al-Raḥmān.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: I.e., beware of the she-camel of Allah. Al-Farrāʾ said: if a reader were to read «ناقة الله» in the nominative, i.e., "this is the she-camel of Allah", it would be permissible. Abū Jaʿfar said: Innovation in the readings is not permissible.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَعَقَرُوها: al-Farrāʾ said: He meant "so they hamstrung her and denied him". This is a mistake regarding the fāʾ, because it indicates that the second comes after the first, and this is the reverse of the language. Moreover, there is no situation here that compels one to it, because they denied Ṣāliḥ when he said to them: "If you hamstring her, Allah will take vengeance on you", so they denied him in what he said and hamstrung her. And it has been said: «فكذبوه» is a complete statement, then فعقروها is conjoined to it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Among the difficulties in this is that it might be said: they had believed and affirmed (him), and had assigned to the she-camel a day and to themselves a day for drinking. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the answer to this is that they acknowledged him but did not believe. This view he stated is one that ought not to be ventured except by a narration, because it is a matter of the unseen, and the narration is contrary to it. Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda, who said: The Uḥaymir of Thamūd held back from hamstringing the she-camel until they all gathered with him in denying Ṣāliḥ — their young and old, their males and females — and for this reason Allah made the punishment general. فَدَمْدَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ بِذَنْبِهِمْ: al-Farrāʾ said: i.e., He caused (the earth) to quake; and others said: i.e., He punished them. فَسَوَّاها: Abū Jaʿfar said: I asked ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān about this pronoun and he said: it refers back to the dumduma (destruction) which دمدم indicated; and someone else said: i.e., He made them equal in the punishment and destroyed them all.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
Thus read the people of Basra and the people of Kufa, and the people of the Ḥijāz read وَلا يَخافُ عُقْباها [Translator's note: the printed vowelling is identical; the Ḥijāzī reading (and that of Ibn ʿĀmir) is فَلا يَخافُ with fāʾ, as the following discussion shows]. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the wāw is better. This is a grave thing to say — that it be said, of what the community read and what appears in the codex (al-sawād) transmitted from the Companions who took it from the Prophet ﷺ, "better" or "best".
Both readings were transmitted by the many from the many, so they are on the level of two verses, because their meanings differ.
Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad Nifṭawayh say: whoever reads with fāʾ, the meaning is for Allah, nothing else. And this is as he said; the exegetes hold this, and it is authentic from Ibn ʿAbbās. Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad said: and whoever reads with wāw holds that the meaning is for the one who hamstrung her, i.e., "the most wretched of them rose up, not fearing its consequence", i.e., and this was his state. What he said is good, except that with the wāw it may not be for Allah, Mighty and Majestic [Translator's note: so the text]. What he said is clear, and Allah knows best what He intended.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: What is well known in the language is that تلاها means "followed it", even though al-Farrāʾ reported that تلاها means "took from it", holding that the moon takes from the light of the sun.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
وَالنَّهارِ إِذا جَلَّاها (3): the apparent and clear meaning is: when it displays the sun, i.e., when it makes it manifest and shows it, because the sun is only ever in it (the daytime); even though al-Farrāʾ said: and the day when it dispels the darkness.
This is a far-fetched view, because the darkness has not been mentioned before.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: The pronoun refers back to the sun as well.

nahhas-irab:5-6.t: وَالسَّماءِ وَما بَناها (5): ما is in the position of the genitive, i.e., "and its building" [Translator's note: i.e., ما is maṣdariyya], and likewise وَالْأَرْضِ وَما طَحاها (6). Ismāʿīl narrated from Abū Khālid, from Abū Ṣāliḥ: طحاها means "spread it out"; and Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: طحاها means "divided it".

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: I.e., its fashioning. Abū Jaʿfar said: whoever said that the meaning is "the One who fashioned it", meaning Allah, Mighty and Majestic — if it were as he said, it would have been ومن.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "He has succeeded whose soul Allah has purified".
